findings.what: TGMsgTopic() wraps the caller's `threadId` as a legacy message thread: `return @{@"@type" : @"messageTopicThread", @"message_thread_id" : @(threadId)};` — but the value every caller actually supplies is a forum_topic_id, not a message_thread_id. TGClient+MessageContent.m:243-244 wraps the very same argument as `@{@"@type" : @"messageTopicForum", @"forum_topic_id" : @(threadId)}`. The two files disagree about the shape of the same value and Messages.m is the wrong one.
findings.failure: TGChatViewController.threadId is assigned at src/TGTopicsViewController.m:1027 from the topic row's @"threadId" key, which TGClient+Forums.m:71-72 fills with `info[@"forum_topic_id"]` (TGClient+Forums.h:6-9 states explicitly that forum_topic_id is an int32 that is NOT a message_thread_id). Forum topic ids are small ints (1, 2, 3...). So sending a message inside a forum topic builds `topic_id = {messageTopicThread, message_thread_id: 3}`. TDLib resolves message_thread_id 3 as a message id, finds no such thread, and answers error 400 "Message thread not found"; -sendText:toChat:thread:replyTo:options:completion: then calls its completion with nil and the message is never sent. The same wrong topic object is used by -forwardMessages:...(line 569), -setDraftText:replyTo:inChat:thread: (line 608), -clearDraftInChat:thread: (line 621) and -sendChatAction:toChat:thread: (line 851), so in a forum topic replies fail, forwards fail, drafts are never stored and the typing indicator never appears.
findings.fix: Change TGMsgTopic to build the forum shape used by the rest of the codebase: `return @{@"@type" : @"messageTopicForum", @"forum_topic_id" : @((int32_t)threadId)};`. Keep it in one place — better still, delete TGMsgTopic and expose the existing TGClient+MessageContent helper, so there is a single definition of "what threadId means". (src/TGClient.m:955-966 -historyForChat:thread: has the same mistake, using threadId as a getMessageThreadHistory message_id; fix that in the same pass or the topic screen loads an empty history.)

findings.what: The entire media/poll/location sending surface of TGClient+MessageContent has no caller anywhere in src/: -sendPhotoAtPath:toChat:thread:caption:spoiler:selfDestructSeconds: (413), -sendAnimationAtPath: (473), -sendAudioAtPath: (493), -sendDocumentAtPath: (519), -sendPhotoAlbumAtPaths:toChat:thread:caption:completion: (540), -sendVenueWithTitle: (592), -sendLiveLocationWithLatitude: (613), -updateLiveLocation: (637), -stopLiveLocation: (656), -sendDice: (665), -sendPollWithQuestion: (675), -stopPoll: (723), -votersForPollOption: (729), -mediaInfoForMessage: (378), -formattedTextForMessage: (334), -editCaptionOfMessage: (354), -parseMarkdown: (293), -entitiesInText: (302), -sendMarkdown: (315), -placeholderTextForContentKind: (397), -mapThumbnailForLatitude: (863), -clickAnimatedEmojiInMessage: (888), -storyForMessage: (905). Verified by grepping every .m/.mm/.h outside TGClient+MessageContent.* — only -sendVideoAtPath:...(440) is reached, from TGChatViewController.m:3063.
findings.failure: The UI hand-rolls raw TDLib dictionaries instead (TGChatViewController.m:2660-2670 and 3076-3090 build `sendMessage` literals). That is exactly how the topic bug above diverged: the inline copies use a `message_thread_id` key that `sendMessage` does not have in the bundled schema (tdlib/td/td/generate/scheme/td_api.tl:12060 `sendMessage chat_id:int53 topic_id:MessageTopic reply_to:... options:... reply_markup:... input_message_content:...`), so a video note or sticker sent from inside a forum topic lands in General. Meanwhile ~900 lines of correct, thread-aware senders sit unreachable and are being kept compiled into a 512MB-device binary.
findings.fix: Either delete the unreachable methods from TGClient+MessageContent.m and its header, or (preferred) route the UI through them: replace the inline `sendMessage` literals at TGChatViewController.m:2660-2670 and 3076-3090 with -mc_send:toChat:thread:completion:, and replace TGChatViewController.m:3720/3735 (`sendVideoAtPath:toChat:` / `sendPhotoAtPath:toChat:`, the thread-less TGClient.m:1229/1278 variants) with the thread-aware MessageContent versions. Do not leave both.

findings.what: mc_sendRequestForChat:thread:content:replyTo: sets a key that does not exist on the request it is building: `request[@"message_thread_id"] = @(threadId);` (repeated at line 581 for sendMessageAlbum). td_api.tl:12060 and :12069 show `sendMessage` and `sendMessageAlbum` carry `topic_id:MessageTopic` and no message_thread_id field at all.
findings.failure: TDLib's generated from_json ignores unknown object fields, so this is silently dropped rather than erroring — which is worse: it reads as a working belt-and-braces fallback and has propagated into the screen files (TGChatViewController.m:2669, 3085) where it is the ONLY thread routing and therefore does nothing, sending topic messages into the chat's General topic.
findings.fix: Delete lines 245 and 581. The `topic_id` dictionary set immediately above each of them is the whole contract.

findings.what: Three independent message flatteners exist for the same TDLib `message` object, each with a different key set: TGMsgBrief (TGClient+Messages.m:52, keys id/text/kind/date/outgoing/senderId), TGSavedFlattenMessage (TGClient+SavedMessages.m:77, keys id/text/date/outgoing/senderId/senderChatId/isPinned/tags — no "kind") and TGFlattenMessage (TGClient.m:625, ~25 keys). The comment at TGClient+Messages.m:50-51 admits the split. The preview helpers are duplicated too: TGSavedPreview (SavedMessages.m:16) vs TGForumsMessagePreview (TGClient+Forums.m) vs the text extraction inside TGMsgBrief. Likewise three error predicates: TGMsgIsError (Messages.m:4), TGMCIsError (MessageContent.m:23) and the inline `![result[@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"error"]` at SavedMessages.m:215/266/321/468.
findings.failure: The dictionaries are not interchangeable. TGMsgBrief sets @"text" to "" for a caption-less photo; TGSavedFlattenMessage sets it to the literal "Photo"; TGFlattenMessage additionally supplies @"kind". Any row renderer fed from the wrong producer either draws the string "Photo" as if it were the user's typed text, or reads a @"kind" that is absent and falls into its text branch. Concretely, -propertiesOfMessage:inChat:completion: (Messages.m:412-415) derives canTranslate from TGMsgBrief's @"text", so a media message whose caption the chat screen displays via TGFlattenMessage still reports canTranslate correctly only by luck of both readers happening to look at content.caption.
findings.fix: Promote one flattener. Move TGFlattenMessage out of TGClient.m's file scope into TGClient+Private.h as `TGFlattenMessage(NSDictionary *)`, delete TGMsgBrief and TGSavedFlattenMessage, and have TGMsgBriefList/savedMessagesTopicHistory call it; keep the Saved-Messages-only extras (senderChatId, isPinned, tags) as a thin wrapper that adds those three keys on top. Same for the error predicate: keep TGMsgIsError in TGClient+Private.h and delete TGMCIsError and the four inline copies.

findings.what: Public methods declared in TGClient+Messages.h with zero callers anywhere in the project: -sendPhotoAlbumAtPaths:toChat:caption:completion: (191), -addLocalTextMessage:toChat:senderUserId:replyTo:completion: (227), -resendMessages:inChat:completion: (256), -replacePhotoInMessage: (324), -replaceVideoInMessage: (343), -unpinAllMessagesInChat: (453), -pinnedMessageIdInChat:completion: (462, reached only by -isMessagePinned: in the same file), -deleteMessagesFromUser: (511), -deleteMessagesInChat:fromDate:toDate: (524), -messageLinkInfoForUrl: (883), -threadForMessage: (930), -readDateOfMessage: (755), -viewersOfMessage: (791), -pressInlineButtonWithData: (984), -rescheduleMessage: (688), -addQuickReplyShortcutNamed: (1066), -sendQuickReplyShortcut: (1086). Also unused in TGClient+SavedMessages.m: -cachedSavedMessagesTopic: (240), -resetSavedMessagesTopicsCache (252), -savedMessagesTopic:messageAtDate:completion: (311), -savedMessagesSparsePositionsForTopic: (329), -pinSavedMessage: (436), -unpinSavedMessage: (446), -unpinAllSavedMessagesWithCompletion: (454), -savedMessagesPinnedMessageWithCompletion: (461), -linkOpensSavedMessages: (504).
findings.failure: No runtime failure — this is pure weight. On a 512MB iPhone 4S with ~40-60MB usable, ~600 lines of unreachable Objective-C plus their selector/method metadata are paged in with the binary for nothing. It also actively misleads: -sendPhotoAlbumAtPaths:toChat:caption:completion: (Messages.m) and -sendPhotoAlbumAtPaths:toChat:thread:caption:completion: (MessageContent.m:540) are two different album senders with incompatible completion types (NSArray* vs NSInteger), and a future caller typing the shorter one silently loses topic routing.
findings.fix: Delete the listed implementations and their header declarations. Keep -pinnedMessageIdInChat:completion: (it is the body of -isMessagePinned:) but make it file-static or move it below a `#pragma mark - private`. If any of these are wanted as future API, move the declarations behind a comment saying so rather than leaving them as apparently-live public surface.

findings.what: -markRead:inChat:source: maps the @"thread" source to the legacy thread constant: `if ([source isEqualToString:@"thread"]) type = @"messageSourceMessageThreadHistory";`. The bundled schema also has `messageSourceForumTopicHistory` (td_api.tl:3186), which is the correct source when the history being viewed is a forum topic — the only kind of thread this app opens (see finding 1).
findings.failure: TDLib uses the message source to decide which unread counter to clear. Marking forum-topic messages read with messageSourceMessageThreadHistory clears the wrong counter, so the topic row in TGTopicsViewController keeps showing an unread badge after the user has read the topic.
findings.fix: Add a branch: `else if ([source isEqualToString:@"topic"]) type = @"messageSourceForumTopicHistory";` and have TGChatViewController pass @"topic" when self.threadId != 0, or simply change the @"thread" mapping to messageSourceForumTopicHistory once finding 1 establishes that threadId is always a forum topic id.

findings.what: TGSavedFlattenTopic resolves the title of a savedMessagesTopicTypeSavedFromChat topic with the user-name cache: `NSString *known = [[TGClient shared] nameForUserId:originChatId];` where originChatId came from `type[@"chat_id"]` (td_api.tl:3867 `savedMessagesTopicTypeSavedFromChat chat_id:int53`).
findings.failure: chat_id for anything forwarded from a group or channel is a negative id (-100...) that is never a key in usersById, so nameForUserId returns nil and @"title" stays @"". TGSavedMessagesViewController then draws a Saved Messages topic row with an empty title for every message forwarded from a channel or group — only forwards from private users get a name.
findings.fix: Fall back to the chat cache when the user lookup misses: after line 130, `if (!title.length) title = [[TGClient shared] titleForChatId:originChatId] ?: @"";` (or issue a getChat for the id and cache it), and only then leave it empty.

findings.what: -loadSavedMessagesTopicsWithLimit:completion: guesses how long TDLib will take to deliver the topics: `dispatch_after(dispatch_time(DISPATCH_TIME_NOW, (int64_t)(0.35 * NSEC_PER_SEC)), dispatch_get_main_queue(), ^{ ... completion(me ? [me cachedSavedMessagesTopics] : ...); });`. loadSavedMessagesTopics returns Ok immediately (td_api.tl:11641) and the actual topics arrive later as updateSavedMessagesTopic updates.
findings.failure: On a cold start on an A5 with a slow network the updates have not arrived after 350ms, so the completion hands back an empty array; TGSavedMessagesViewController.m:536 then calls -applyTopics:@[] and stops the spinner, showing an empty Saved Messages screen. It self-heals only because the screen also installs a topics-changed handler in viewWillAppear — if that handler has been nil'd by a second controller's dealloc (line 421 nils the single file-static slot unconditionally), the empty state is permanent until the user leaves and re-enters.
findings.fix: Drop the dispatch_after. Call the completion synchronously with the current cache and rely on the topics-changed handler for the fill-in; and make -setSavedMessagesTopicsChangedHandler: keyed per observer (or have TGSavedMessagesViewController's dealloc only clear the slot when it still owns it) so one controller's dealloc cannot silence another's.
